title: Origin of the inhomogeneous linewidth in a solid state $^{229}$Th:CaF$_2$ nuclear clock
authors: Kai Li, Tian Ooi, Jack F. Doyle, Konstantin Herb, Emil Pellett, Martin Pimon, Thorsten Schumm, Steven M. Girvin, Leo Radzihovsky, Jun Ye
abstract: Narrow linewidth (high-Q) quantum discriminators are essential for realizing solid-state $^{229}$Th nuclear clocks, yet the observed transition linewidths remain at the tens-to-hundreds-of-kilohertz level, far exceeding the sub-Hertz linewidth set by the radiative lifetime of the nuclear isomer. Here, we investigate the origin of this broadening in $^{229}$Th:CaF$_2$ through systematic measurements of the linewidth as functions of temperature, thorium concentration, and quadrupole state, accompanied by theoretical analysis and first-principle simulations. We find that the linewidth is independent of temperature, increases linearly with thorium concentration, and depends strongly on the quadrupole state. Data analysis identifies variations of the local electric-field gradient (EFG) as the dominant source of inhomogeneous broadening and reveals that the EFG disorder increases linearly with thorium concentration. The observed Lorentzian line shapes and linewidth linear concentration dependence are explained naturally from the $1/r^3$ scaling of a random distribution of long-range dopant-induced perturbations. Complementary atomistic and \textit{ab initio} density-functional-theory calculations reproduce these characteristic features and provide insights into the microscopic defect configurations responsible for the broadening. These results establish the dominant broadening mechanism in solid-state $^{229}$Th and provide guidance for engineering nuclear-clock materials with reduced inhomogeneous broadening.
summary: This paper characterizes the source of inhomogeneous broadening in solid-state $^{229}	ext{Th}$ nuclear clocks embedded in $	ext{CaF}_2$. By measuring linewidths across varying conditions, the authors determine that the broadening is dominated by static, random variations in the local Electric-Field Gradient (EFG). The study provides both experimental evidence and DFT simulations confirming that this EFG disorder scales linearly with dopant concentration, offering crucial guidance for material engineering.
main_problem: The study investigates the origin of the large inhomogeneous linewidth observed in solid-state $^{229}	ext{Th}:	ext{CaF}_2$ nuclear clocks, which significantly exceeds the natural linewidth.
main_result: The dominant source of broadening is identified as variations in the local Electric-Field Gradient (EFG), which increases linearly with the thorium dopant concentration.
method: The research combines systematic experimental measurements of linewidths versus temperature and concentration with theoretical modeling using first-principle DFT calculations.
model_or_system: The system is the $^{229}	ext{Th}$ nuclear transition in a $	ext{CaF}_2$ crystal host, governed by interactions involving the isomeric shift and the local EFG. The broadening is modeled using the statistical distribution of EFG variations.
key_observables: Linewidth ($\Gamma$) as a function of temperature, thorium concentration, and quadrupole state; frequency shifts related to EFG components ($V_{zz}, V_{yy}$).
important_parameters: Linear dependence of linewidth on Th concentration; $1/r^3$ scaling for long-range dopant perturbations; EFG ratios ($\Gamma_{yy}/\Gamma_{zz} \sim 1.6$).
main_assumptions: The dominant broadening mechanism is attributed to static, long-range, dopant-induced variations in the local EFG, which are assumed to follow a specific statistical distribution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of linewidths on various parameters and show schematic representations of how the surrounding charge distribution influences both the isomeric shift and the local EFG.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from observing the linewidth discrepancy to systematically measuring its dependence on external parameters (T, concentration), identifying EFG disorder as the cause, and finally providing theoretical explanations and computational verification using DFT.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the fundamental limitations of solid-state quantum sensors by pinpointing the microscopic source of decoherence (EFG disorder) and providing a quantitative model for its engineering mitigation.

FIG. 4. The fitting results with coupling ρ = −0.6. (a) Opti- mized EFG variations Γzz and Γyy obtained from the fit. Both scale linearly with the 229Th concentration. (b) Comparison of measured and model predicted linewidths. Extrapolation the linewidth vs. concentration shows that the linewidths of all four transitions converge to a common point, indicating the zero-doping broadening is also arising from EFG disorder in the host crystal.

FIG. 5. Linewidths calculated from ab initio theory as a function of 229Th concentration for the (a) C3v, (b) vCa, and (c) dimer configurations. Experimental (filled) and theory (open) data points share the same symbol for each quadrupole component, the dotted lines are linear fits to theory. Among the three configurations, only the dimer reproduces the experimentally observed hierarchy of concentration-dependent transition linewidths, although the calculated linewidths are approximately an order of magnitude larger than the measured values and are therefore scaled by a factor of ∼0.06.
